newsitem.title: UK: Beckett to visit Japan, back investors in UK.
newsitem.headline: Beckett to visit Japan, back investors in UK.

text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary, Margaret Beckett, will visit Japan next week and tell the country's leading investors in the UK that the new Labour government will support them strongly, she said on Wednesday.
Beckett will fly to Tokyo on May 26 for a three-day visit, her first trip abroad since her appointment following the May 1 British election.

She said in a statement: "The economic relationship between the UK and Japan is vitally important. A key element of my visit will be to brief Japan's leading investors in the UK on the new Government's continuing strong support for them."
Beckett's department said during her visit she will have meetings with Japan's ministers of Finance and International Trade and Industry (MITI).
She will also meet Shoichiro Toyoda, Chairman of the Keidanren business lobby and of Toyota Motor Corp. Toyota has a carmaking plant in Derbyshire, central England and an engine plant in North Wales.

During the election, the Conservatives, now in opposition, claimed that a Labour government would lead to a fall-off in inward investment to Britain because of the party's plans to introduce a minimum wage, increase trade union rights and sign up to European Union workplace standards. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
